page: Microsoft Azure E128s_v7 is an Esv7-family virtual machine configured with 128 vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, the server features 64 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The processor architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core stress-ng CPU performance falls within the average range, multi-core stress-ng CPU performance ranks in the top tier. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 704.78 GB/sec, whereas single-threaded bzip3 decompression is in the top 25%. The system demonstrates exceptional throughput in database and web serving workloads, achieving 189.85 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 165.05 GB/sec in static web serving. For large language model inference, the server processes prompts efficiently, reaching top-tier speeds of 45.31 tokens/second for a 70B model, though text generation speeds remain average.

Given its high resource density and dedicated compute allocation, the E128s_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads that can leverage its massive 1 TB RAM footprint and 128 vCPUs without the overhead of local storage. The absence of bundled local disks means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale Premium Storage independently. This profile is suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, multi-threaded data processing pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.
